arcade-text.create: Make a text label that you can move like a sprite. Use its text blocks to change the words later.
arcade-text.setText: Change the words on this label. Its picture resizes to fit the new text.
arcade-text.setMaxFontHeight: Choose how tall the label's letters can be, in pixels. This uses Arcade's built-in fonts.
arcade-text.setBorder: Add a colored border and space around this text label.
arcade-text.setOutline: Draw a colored line around the letters so they stand out from the background.
arcade-text.setIcon: Put a small picture beside this label's words.

arcade-timers.after: Run the code inside after this many milliseconds. The rest of your game keeps running while it waits.
arcade-timers.debounce: Wait until calls with this name stop for this long, then run the code once. Useful for finishing a repeated action.
arcade-timers.throttle: Run the code now, then ignore more calls with the same name until this wait time ends. Useful for a firing cooldown.

pxt-lantern.startLanternEffect: Darken the room and keep a circle of light around this sprite.
pxt-lantern.stopLanternEffect: Remove the single lantern effect and show the room normally again.
pxt-lantern.setLightBandWidth: Choose how wide each ring of the lantern's light is, in pixels.
pxt-lantern.setBreathingEnabled: Make the lantern's light gently grow and shrink, or keep it steady.
pxt-lantern.toggleLighting: Turn room lighting on or off. Add light sources to sprites to light up parts of the dark room.
pxt-lantern.addLightSource: Make a circle of light follow this sprite. Turn lighting on to see the dark areas around it.
pxt-lantern.removeLightSource: Stop this sprite from lighting up the room.
pxt-lantern.bandWidthOf: Change how quickly this sprite's light gets darker toward its edge. A larger number makes a wider light.
pxt-lantern.addFlashLightSource: Attach a cone of light to this sprite. Choose its direction, distance and width.
pxt-lantern.flashlightSourceAttachedTo: Get the flashlight attached to this sprite so you can change it.

arcade-block-objects.blockObject.create: Make an empty object to keep related game information together.
arcade-block-objects.storeOnSprite: Attach this object to a sprite so its information travels with the character or item.
arcade-block-objects.getStoredObject: Get the object previously attached to this sprite.

arcade-mini-menu.insertMenuItem: Add a new choice at the end of this menu. Expand the block to choose a position; zero is the first choice.

pxt-sound-effects.createSound: Make a retro sound that changes pitch and volume over time. Duration is in milliseconds; pitch is in hertz.
pxt-sound-effects.play: Play this sound effect and let the rest of your code continue.
pxt-sound-effects.playUntilDone: Play this sound effect and wait until it finishes before continuing.
pxt-sound-effects.loop: Repeat this sound effect until its stop block is used.
pxt-sound-effects.stop: Stop this sound effect's repeating playback.

pxt-raycasting.setViewMode: Choose the normal top-down game view or a first-person view of your tilemap. The first-person renderer starts only when its blocks are used.
pxt-raycasting.getRenderSpriteVariable: Get the character whose eyes form the first-person camera. Place and move it with the usual sprite blocks.
pxt-raycasting.isViewMode: True when the game is showing this type of view.
pxt-raycasting.setViewAngleInDegree: Turn the first-person camera to this angle, in degrees. Zero looks right and 90 looks down.

arcade-shadowcasting.setAnchor: Choose the character whose view lights the map. Wall tiles hide the areas behind them.
arcade-shadowcasting.setShadowEnabled: Turn wall-blocking shadows on or off. Set an anchor character and tilemap first.
arcade-shadowcasting.setShadowColor: Choose the color used for hidden parts of the map when the shadow mode is fill.

pxt-status-bar.statusbars.create: Make a sprite that displays a value as a bar. Attach it to a character for health or energy, then change its value and maximum.
pxt-status-bar.StatusBarSprite.setColor: Choose the colors for the filled and empty parts of this bar. The value and maximum decide how much is filled.
pxt-status-bar.StatusBarSprite.setBarBorder: Draw a border around this bar. Choose its thickness in pixels and its color.
pxt-status-bar.StatusBarSprite.setLabel: Show this short label beside the bar, in the chosen color.
pxt-status-bar.StatusBarSprite.setBarSize: Change the width and height of this bar, in pixels.
